      "title": "MetricAlertDetectorHandler is abstract and cannot be instantiated",
      "body": "StatefulDetectorHandler requires implementations for counter_names, get_dedupe_value, get_group_key_values, and build_occurrence_and_event_data, but MetricAlertDetectorHandler only contains pass. Detector.detector_handler instantiates group_type.detector_handler(self), so any Detector whose type is metric_alert_fire will raise TypeError at runtime instead of returning a handler or being skipped. This is a regression from the previous stub, which implemented evaluate and was instantiable."
    },
    {
      "file": "src/sentry/workflow_engine/processors/detector.py",

      "severity": "medium",

      "title": "get_state_data crashes when counter_names is empty",
      "body": "StatefulDetectorHandler.get_state_data initializes counter_updates to {} and only populates it when self.counter_names is truthy. It later unconditionally accesses counter_updates[gk] for every requested group key. If a valid stateful detector has no counters (counter_names == []), this raises KeyError. It should fall back to an empty dict per group key, e.g. counter_updates.get(gk, {})."
    },
    {
      "file": "tests/sentry/workflow_engine/processors/test_detector.py",

      "body": "In TestEvaluateGroupKeyValue.test_dedupe, the expected occurrence is built with group key \"val1\" and value 6, but the code under test evaluates group key \"group_key\" with value 10. Because build_mock_occurrence_and_event uses the group key in the occurrence fingerprint, the expected result does not match the actual occurrence produced by evaluate_group_key_value. This looks like a copy/paste error and makes the test unreliable or invalid."

The annotation should be dict[DetectorGroupKey, int] to avoid misleading implementers and type-checking errors for valid handlers that return None keys."

findings.title: MetricAlertDetectorHandler is abstract and cannot be instantiated
findings.body: StatefulDetectorHandler requires implementations for counter_names, get_dedupe_value, get_group_key_values, and build_occurrence_and_event_data, but MetricAlertDetectorHandler only contains pass. Detector.detector_handler instantiates group_type.detector_handler(self), so any Detector whose type is metric_alert_fire will raise TypeError at runtime instead of returning a handler or being skipped. This is a regression from the previous stub, which implemented evaluate and was instantiable.

findings.title: get_state_data crashes when counter_names is empty
findings.body: StatefulDetectorHandler.get_state_data initializes counter_updates to {} and only populates it when self.counter_names is truthy. It later unconditionally accesses counter_updates[gk] for every requested group key. If a valid stateful detector has no counters (counter_names == []), this raises KeyError. It should fall back to an empty dict per group key, e.g. counter_updates.get(gk, {}).

findings.title: Expected occurrence is built with the wrong group key and value
findings.body: In TestEvaluateGroupKeyValue.test_dedupe, the expected occurrence is built with group key "val1" and value 6, but the code under test evaluates group key "group_key" with value 10. Because build_mock_occurrence_and_event uses the group key in the occurrence fingerprint, the expected result does not match the actual occurrence produced by evaluate_group_key_value. This looks like a copy/paste error and makes the test unreliable or invalid.

findings.title: get_group_key_values type annotation does not match allowed group keys
findings.body: StatefulDetectorHandler.get_group_key_values is annotated as returning dict[str, int], but DetectorGroupKey is used elsewhere and the tests/key builders explicitly support None as a group key. The annotation should be dict[DetectorGroupKey, int] to avoid misleading implementers and type-checking errors for valid handlers that return None keys.

findings.title: evaluate docstring still says it returns a list
findings.body: StatefulDetectorHandler.evaluate now returns dict[DetectorGroupKey, DetectorEvaluationResult], but its docstring still says it returns a list of DetectorEvaluationResult. The docstring should be updated to describe the new dict return shape.
